name: showcase_water_sphere
_comment: Native PhysicsView port of the Blender crystal_sph_addon preset SHOWCASE_WATER_SPHERE
(docs/todo/PLAN_sph_showcase_water_sphere.md): water pours from an emitter inside an
invisible closed SphereBoundary (radius 0.25m) until it fills to 68% (~354k particles),
then settles for the final 33 frames. Same axis conversion as showcase_dam_break.json.
The emitter used to destabilize around frame 26-40: splashback off the empty sphere's
floor came back up at 2.4x its own ballistic limit and climbed all the way to the
emitter. Fixed in Physics -- see docs/issue/water_sphere_showcase_emitter_instability.md
sections 9 and 11. Two things did it: the wall's density contribution now only fills a
particle's deficit instead of being added unconditionally (section 9), and the
viscosity below is no longer halved along with the particle radius (section 11 -- that
one is what this production tier was still failing on). SetFluidBoundaryDamping below
is a third, much smaller contributor; see its own label. That investigation also found the Blender addon has a
separate bug where the emitter ends up at the sphere's center (world origin) instead
of the designed (0.04,0,0.15) -- this scenario uses the DESIGNED position (native
(0.04,0.15,0.0)), since that bug is presets.py/sim_core.py-specific (matrix_world
vs. local-vertex handling) and doesn't exist in this native port, which sets the
emitter center directly via AddEmitter.
emit_rate/emit_max_particles are computed the same way presets.py computes them
(flow = pi*jet_radius^2*jet_speed; rate = flow/spacing^3; max_particles =
fill_volume/spacing^3) rather than copied from the design doc's rounded prose values.
emit_speed_jitter (0.02 in the addon) isn't reproduced -- AddEmitter doesn't expose
it (see CommandDispatcher.h), so this scenario gets the native Emitter default (0.1)
instead; a bit more velocity spread in the jet than the addon's tuned value.
PhysicsView.exe --run-scenario scenarios/showcase/showcase_water_sphere.json

steps.label: Liveness check
WCSPH (only solver SphereBoundary's density contribution is implemented for)
particle_radius=0.0025
effect_length_factor=4.0 -> effectLength=4*radius=0.01
rest_density=1000 kg/m^3

viscosity_coe=0.010 -- same as the preview tier on purpose: viscosityCoe is a kinematic viscosity (m^2/s) and must NOT be rescaled with the particle radius. At the 0.005 this used to carry, the jet hitting the dry sphere peaked at 1.53x its ballistic limit and threw spray past the emitter by frame 14 (docs/issue/water_sphere_showcase_emitter_instability.md section 11)
tension_coe=0.0
pressure_coe_scale=20.0 -- raised from the addon default 1.96 to hold the 0.31m-deep final pool (design doc section 4.1)
time_step=0.00015
gravity (0,0,-9.8) Blender -> (0,-9.8,0) native

wall damping 0.35: takes the restitution off the wall penalty spring, which on its own has a measured coefficient of restitution of 1.03. Kept because it costs nothing, but it is NOT what fixed this scene -- with the density clamp and viscosity right, particles penetrate the wall by only ~5% of h and zeta changes peak speed by under 1% at this tier (docs/issue/water_sphere_showcase_emitter_instability.md section 11.5)
boundary_min/max (-0.30,-0.30,-0.35)/(0.30,0.30,0.30) Blender -> native

empty at frame 1: degenerate (zero-size) box seeds at most 1 particle at the origin (same convention as scenarios/61_emit_dfsph_faucet.json), filled from there entirely by the emitter -- Box3d's constructor normalizes min/max, so an inverted box collapses to the default (0,0,0)-(20,20,20) instead of seeding nothing
no box/sphere source regions either
clear any previous sphere boundary
Water Sphere container: center (0,0,0) r=0.25 max_penetration=0.02 Blender -> native (center unchanged, it's the origin)
1 sphere boundary registered
emitter budget: fill volume (68% of the sphere, z=+0.06) / spacing^3 = pi*(R^2 z - z^3/3 + 2R^3/3) / 0.005^3
rebuild: 0 particles, sphere boundary + max-particle budget now active
precondition: starts essentially empty (0 or 1 particle, see the degenerate-box note above)
Inflow emitter: center (0.04,0,0.15) r=0.075 dir=(0,0,-1) speed=2.45 Blender -> native center (0.04,0.15,0.0) dir (0,-1,0); rate = pi*0.075^2*2.45/0.005^3
1 emitter registered
PLY sequence output directory (gitignored screenshots/)

bake 240 frames x 33 substeps = 7920 physics steps (1 frame = 33*1.5e-4 = 4.95ms physical time), one PLY per frame -- filling stops on its own around frame ~207 once SetFluidMaxParticles' budget is reached
change: the sphere has filled -- particle count grew from the empty start
invariant: didn't exceed the emitter's budget
